title: Outbound: how does the draft claim suppress a concurrent double Send?
scope: Two Today tabs sending one draft, the Next.js server action, and the conditional Postgres claim on its row.
omissions: Guards and Gmail/LinkedIn/X delivery that run after a successful claim
Conversation Send: each click inserts its own row, so no shared claim

notes.title: The claim is one conditional UPDATE
notes.text: UPDATE sets sending, clears error, stamps sentAt/updatedAt, saves edits WHERE id, out, status IN (draft,failed) RETURNING. A concurrent UPDATE then matches 0 rows → skipped.

notes.title: Suppression, not exactly-once
notes.text: Winner's outcome arrives after guards/delivery. Throws and most guards set failed, claimable again, even if markSent throws after Gmail accepted; closed/replied set skipped.

notes.title: Crash after claim strands the row
notes.text: If the function dies after the claim, the row stays 'sending': Send/Skip match only draft|failed; refresh only resolves LinkedIn rows with a run id. Today shows it 'Queued on LinkedIn'.
